findings.why: The 25 cells the HRE ledger gave to Cliopatria's Trier row in 1431 have no cell in common with the 33-cell Moselle corridor the Trier dossier substitutes for all ten Cliopatria Trier shapes (the misplaced block in Bavaria and the Hunsrueck-Nahe country). The Electorate of Trier page puts the electorate 'along the river Moselle between Trier, near the French border, and Koblenz on the Rhine' and records no gain in 1431 or the 15th century, so the event had no page behind it and, once the Trier corrections compile, left the 25 cells (Rhineland-Palatinate 21, Baden-Wurttemberg 2, Saarland 1, Bas-Rhin 1) with no owner from 1431 to 1647. They now stay in the Empire's shape; 1619-1647 rests on the dossier's own treatment of occupied land, not a new page.

The Cote-d'Or / Saone-et-Loire strip is already excluded: every 'wrong' Arles keyframe 1034-1375 is replaced by the 1033 extent less the pieces that left. A ghost shell would need all shell keyframes emptied and an undated 1260 loss event; the page dates nothing there ('Imperial kingdom of the Holy Roman Empire', 'one of the empire's three constituent realms', territories with 'considerable autonomy', imperial rule 'mainly nominal' since the 14th century). The shell is wholly covered by the Empire's shape or smaller states in every keyframe year 1260-1375, and R3 tints the few cells Arles takes from the Empire (102 cell-years, 4 years) as constituent of the Empire, i.e. in the Empire's colour. hierarchy.csv supplies it.

Confirmed on the pages: after the 1301 Treaty of Bruges Henry III was 'forced to recognise all of his county west of the river Meuse as a fief of France' (Duchy of Bar) and 'paid homage to Philip for part of his lands', 'then called the Barrois mouvant' (Henry III page); 'From 1480, it was united to the imperial Duchy of Lorraine'. duchy-of-bar already has the 1297 contest_start and 1301 contest_end and its notes ask for the France event; the missing vassal_start is in kingdom-of-france, which is not mine. The pages do not say when French overlordship ended, so the vassal_end at 1480 follows the Bar dossier's own merge.

The 32 Artois cells never overlap the Empire's shape (0 cells 1326-1375), so R3 never arbitrates them; only the constituent tint reaches them, because it covers all of the Free County's direct cells from the 1329 Artois gain. Page: 'Upon her death in 1329, Artois passed to her daughter ... Countess Joan II'; infobox 'Fiefdom of France'; the Empire link appears only from 1493. Both remedies (end county-of-artois at the 1329 transfer so the Free County keyframe of 1329 takes over; or split Artois out of the Free County) need county-of-artois, which is not mine, and dropping Artois from the Free County alone would leave 32 cells unowned from 1333, so free-county-of-burgundy was left unchanged.
